text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text commentary of the Premier League showdown between Tottenham and West Ham.
Fifth place plays ninth in this tasty London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
The hosts are desperate to end a run of four straight matches without a win, while their visitors are unbeaten in five across all competitions.
Ange Postecoglou makes two changes from Spurs' entertaining 3-3 draw with Manchester City last weekend.
Romero returns from a three-match suspension in the heart of defence, with Emerson dropping to the bench.
Hojbjerg also comes into the starting XI in place of Gil, who is named among the substitutes.
A lengthy injury list features the likes of James Maddison, Eric Dier, Micky van de Ven and Ivan Perisic.
David Moyes also makes two alterations from West Ham.
Zouma returns to captain the Hammers in the heart of defence after missing the weekend draw with Crystal Palace following a burglary at his home.
The other change comes in goal with Fabianski making his first Premier League start of the season.
He replaces Alphonse Areola, who injured his wrist in training on Wednesday.
The visitors remain without Michail Antonio, who is still coming back from a knee injury.
Tottenham have prevailed in three of their last four Premier League meetings with West Ham on this ground.
Although, the Hammers do have fond memories of this fixture, having inflicted Spurs' first league defeat at their new home courtesy of a 1-0 victory in April 2019.
The teams make their way out onto the pitch and we are fast approaching kick-off at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Referee Michael Salisbury blows his whistle and Tottenham get the match under way.
The hosts go straight onto the attack as Udogie wins possession high up the field.
He finds Son, who in turn slips the ball through for Kulusevski on the edge of the box.
The latter goes to ground after colliding with Fabianski, but a goal-kick is given.
He appeared to be in an offside position anyway, so any goal would likely not have counted.
Spurs threaten again following a corner.
After their first threat is dealt with, Porro whips a delicious ball into the box from the left flank.
However, Fabianski is alert and gathers from the air.
A comedic moment sees Hojbjerg fall to the ground after getting his feet in a proper tangle inside the box.
Sarcastic cheers can be heard from the away end, and it is one of those moments the Spurs midfielder would have hoped not many people saw!
Of course, Tottenham have lost both their last two Premier League home games.
You must go back to September 2008 under Juande Ramos for the last time they suffered three successive defeats on home soil.
Enjoying over 90 per cent of the possession, it has been a thoroughly dominant start by Spurs.
Although, West Ham are doing well to maintain their concentration levels at the moment.

ROMERO!!! 1-0 TOTTENHAM! Welcome back! Just 11 minutes into his return, Romero makes just the impact he would have wanted! The centre-half rises above Alvarez and Aguerd to meet Porro's corner, and firmly plant a header beyond Fabianski.
Porro's corner was precise and begging to be attacked.
Romero duly obliged.
West Ham look to respond immediately and Kudus finds himself in an advanced position, but the offside flag stops him in his tracks.
Although it did not end in a goal, West Ham will be encouraged by that response.
The Hammers have been very much on the back foot so far, and must look to gain a foothold in the contest.
Tottenham attack again and space opens for Son to take aim from the edge of the area.
But the Spurs skipper sends his attempt straight into Fabianski's arms.
West Ham are awarded a corner and Ward-Prowse whips a dangerous delivery into the six-yard box.
Zouma attacks it, but cannot quite keep his header on target under pressure from the goalkeeper.
It looks more like a basketball contest at the moment with both sides taking turns attacking.
Following a neat exchange of passes, Lo Celso tries his luck from distance, but his attempt is high and wide of the target.
Tottenham are still a goal to the good at the midway point of an entertaining first half.
Romero's header separates the sides, but both are looking dangerous going forward.
Kudus dispossesses Udogie deep inside the Tottenham half and goes for goal from range.
It is on target, but never troubling Vicario.
Following Romero's header, West Ham have now failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 12 away Premier League matches.
Although, the Hammers will be encouraged by the fact they have scored at least once in their last eight such games.
West Ham look to counter and Ward-Prowse quickly switches the play to Paqueta.
But the latter's touch is too heavy and Spurs can clear their lines.
Kudus is one-on-one with Vicario after latching onto a throughball, but drags his shot wide of the target.
However, his blushes are somewhat spared by the late raising of the offside flag.
There is a concern for West Ham as Paqueta stays down and is in need of attention.
The medical team enter the pitch to tend to the midfielder.
SAVE! After Paqueta makes his way to the sidelines, Tottenham look to capitalise on their brief numerical advantage.
The ball sits up nicely for Lo Celso to strike on the volley from the edge of the box, but Fabianski does well to beat it away.
Spurs maintain their threat with West Ham struggling to get out.
Johnson latches onto a clever throughball into the box, but he shoots straight at Fabianski from a tight angle.
West Ham survive again.
Fabianski can only punch Lo Celso's cross straight to Kulusevski, whose shot is blocked by Emerson, before Bissouma eventually sends the follow-up attempt over.
The Hammers look to respond before half-time.
Kudus skips inside from the right wing and evades a couple of challenges.
He then looks for Paqueta, who is unable to accept his pass due to being in an offside position, and that takes the sting out of the visitors' threat.
We are into the final minute of regulation time in this first half.
Can Tottenham hold out until the break or can West Ham find an equaliser?
There will be two additional minutes played at the end of this first half.
OFF THE POST! Almost an own goal by Zouma! Tottenham push for a second goal and the ball is neatly worked out to Lo Celso, who fires it into the six-yard box.
Having to cut it out, a sliding Zouma sees the ball ricochet off him and onto the left post with Fabianski beaten.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-0 WEST HAM
Tottenham lead West Ham by a goal to nil at the midway point in this London derby.
Romero marked his return from suspension by opening the scoring from a header in the 11th minute.
The hosts almost went 2-0 up in first-half stoppage time, when Zouma turned Lo Celso's cross dangerously against his own post.
Although they lead, Spurs will be disappointed not to be heading into the break with a healthier advantage.
Indeed, they dominated large periods of the first half with over three quarters of the possession, while registering 13 shots on goal to their opponents' four.
We are off and running again as West Ham get the ball rolling once more.
Tottenham maintain the pressure following a corner.
Porro plays a neat one-two with Lo Celso and looks for the far corner, but there is just too much elevation on his attempt.
Spurs have won just three of their last nine home midweek Premier League matches, having prevailed in 14 of their previous 15 such games.
BOWEN!!! 1-1! Smash and grab from West Ham! The visitors equalise out of nowhere.
Bowen is initially involved as they quickly counter.
Kudus lines up a shot and his attempt ricochets off both Tottenham centre-halves before falling kindly for Bowen, who calmly lifts the ball into the roof of the net.

events.action: lifts the ball into the roof of the net

text: It is a landmark goal for Bowen, who scores for West Ham for the 50th time in all competitions.
It is also the seventh successive Premier League away match in which he has found the net.
West Ham have their tails up as they look to turn this contest on its head.
Coufal shows great strength as he outmuscles Udogie and finds Bowen.
He and Ward-Prowse combine to tee up Paqueta, but his precise attempt is read by Vicario.
Emerson receives the first yellow card of the game for bringing down Porro on Tottenham's right flank.
Porro goes in late on Paqueta and the right-back can have no complaints as his name goes into the book.
This contest is finely poised as we pass the hour mark at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
It really could go either way.
Vicario produces a smart reflex save to deny Soucek's volley from point-blank range.
However, it would not have counted as the midfielder was offside as he made the move to connect with Coufal's cross.
Bowen's equaliser was his seventh away goal in the Premier League this season.
No West Ham player has ever scored more in a single campaign, as he matches the tally of Trevor Morley (1993-94) and Paulo Wanchope (1999-2000).
Tottenham make a double change.
The first of these sees Richarlison brought on in place of Hojbjerg.
The hosts' other change sees Lo Celso make way to be replaced by Skipp in the middle of the park.
There is concern for West Ham, who lost Areola to injury on Wednesday, as Fabianski stays down.
Thankfully, the latter is soon back on his feet and able to continue.
CHANCE! Richarlison should score! The substitute is unmarked in the six-yard box as he connects with Porro's deep cross at the far post.
However, he can only head wide with only Fabianski to beat.
GOOD SAVE! Spurs continue to apply the pressure and a patient build-up culminates in Porro getting a shot away.
But Fabianski is alert at his near post to beat the attempt to safety.
WARD-PROWSE!!! 2-1 WEST HAM! The turnaround is complete! Vicario is forced to dash off his line to prevent Bowen from latching onto Udogie's short backpass.
But in doing so, he sends it straight to Ward-Prowse, who hits the post, but is completely unchallenged as he subsequently tucks the rebound into the empty net.

events.action: tucks the rebound into the empty net

text: Suddenly, West Ham lead at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
As things stand, the Hammers are on course for only their second victory in 11 Premier League London derbies away from home.
Spurs look to respond and Son whips a free-kick into the box from the left flank.
However, Paqueta is alert at the near post and heads the ball to safety.
Ward-Prowse goes into the book after a challenge on Richarlison.
Can Son stand up and be counted for Tottenham? The skipper has been directly involved in eight goals in his eight Premier League home games against West Ham, scoring five and assisting three.
He has also found the net in his last three such matches.
Spurs make a couple more changes.
The first of them sees Bissouma make way to be replaced by Gil.
Johnson is the other player to make way for Spurs.
Sarr comes on in his place for the final six minutes.
West Ham push for a third goal that would surely put the game beyond Tottenham.
Ward-Prowse sends a corner into the six-yard box, but the hosts just about scramble the ball away.
Son, who was unable to build on his impressive streak against West Ham, makes way with Veliz taking his place for the latter stages.
There is also activity on the West Ham bench.
Kudus is given a breather with Fornals coming on in midfield.
Desperate to win the ball from Bowen, Romero goes in strong and catches the West Ham forward late.
He goes into the book as a result.
The fourth official indicates there will be a minimum of five additional minutes at the end of this game.
There is still time for Tottenham, but can West Ham hang on?
Alvarez is shown a yellow card as West Ham desperately try to hold out for all three points.
Time is runnng out for Tottenham, but they are awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box after Bowen trips Porro.
Can the hosts make the most of this?
Porro's free-kick strikes Zouma and deflects behind for a corner.
Spurs claim it hit the West Ham skipper on the arm, but a VAR check quickly rules that out.
Kulusevski goes into the book after a foul on Paqueta.
West Ham are nearly there.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-2 WEST HAM
West Ham come from behind to heap more misery on Tottenham by snatching a 2-1 derby victory.
Spurs led at half-time thanks to Romero's 11th-minute header.
However, the Hammers hit back after the interval, Bowen equalising within seven minutes of the restart.
The visitors then completed the turnaround 16 minutes from time when Ward-Prowse slotted into an empty net following a mix-up between Udogie and Vicario.

West Ham will look to maintain their six-match unbeaten streak when they travel to Fulham on Sunday, while Tottenham will look to end their five-game winless run when they host Newcastle United on the same day.
That's all for today.
Thank you for following our coverage.
Until next time, goodbye!
